structure: A JSON backlog, not prose: workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/dr1-parity-union/backlog.json (31,988 lines), the Design Release 1 parity backlog of run EUDPA-328-DR1U (target live-animals-frontend, corpus dr1u), copied from commit 6688fd8e on origin/feat/parity-report-triage-view. Top level: run_id, target, corpus and increments[], an array of 161 rows (inc-001 to inc-161, not in id order; the file runs roughly by domain: service-wide, dashboard, origin, commodities, identification, addresses, import-reason, hub, documents, transport, contact, address-book, review, then a tail of hub/dashboard/dropped rows). Each row is one difference between the real animals frontend and the DR1 prototype, with fields id, title, status, domain, slice, band, type, confidence, finding {frontend, prototype, difference, correction, falsifiedBy, relatedTo}, detail (the finding restated as prose), evidence, screens, citations, controls, dependsOn, provenance {sourceA, sourceC, origin, note, better, judged} (how two discovery runs were matched), commit, branch, ticket, prs, gate (always null), milestone (always null), failure_reason, and on some rows decision {ruling, note} (44 rows), notes (4 rows), openQuestions (17 rows) and repo (4 rows). Statuses: 118 done, 34 blocked, 5 dropped, 3 deferred, 1 rejected. Each row is about 120 to 300 lines; inc-161 is 865. The scope takes in only DR1's judgements, so the parts cover the 64 rows that carry one: every row whose status is blocked, dropped, deferred or rejected (43 rows, each with a decision giving the reason), and every done row with a non-null decision, notes, openQuestions or failure_reason (21 rows: inc-003, 004, 006, 007, 033, 067, 069, 079, 082, 087, 091, 118, 122, 136, 137, 138, 146, 147, 150, 153, 161). Left out: the 97 done rows with none of those fields, whose finding.difference is a built proposal rather than a judgement (inc-051's finding argues for keeping the frontend's nine-digit CPH check, but in finding rather than notes, so it stays out); and on in-scope rows, provenance notes about how runs A and C were matched, PR and commit bookkeeping, evidence and screens, which the part agents read for context but do not claim as judgements. The parts are cut along the backlog's own domain seams, each row read in full by its line range.

parts.title: Service-wide rows
parts.scope: The six in-scope service-wide rows: inc-003, inc-004, inc-007, inc-006, inc-161 (done) and inc-013 (dropped). Stops at the dashboard rows.
read: backlog.json top-level run_id, target and corpus
covers: inc-003 (phase banner): every RULING and decision in its notes and openQuestions
inc-004 (section caption above headings) and inc-007 (service navigation items): every decision and open question in their openQuestions
inc-006 (save and cancel controls): the choice recorded in its notes
inc-161 (what a page offers at its foot): its decision.ruling and decision.note
inc-013 (save-and-return button and cancel link): why it was dropped, from its decision

parts.title: Dashboard list, filters, search and sort
parts.scope: Eight blocked dashboard rows about how the notification list is filtered, searched, sorted and headed: inc-017, 018, 019, 020, 021, 022, 023, 024. The other dashboard rows are part 3.
covers: The 8 blocked rows inc-017 (date filter), 018 (grouped collapsed filters), 019 (three-term search), 020 (status filter), 021 (list heading), 022 (results count), 023 (sort options), 024 (sort applies only on submit): each row's decision.ruling, who blocked it and when, and the reason in decision.note, with the difference it blocks named from finding.difference
Any condition the notes set for reopening, such as a fresh ruling if the dashboard stays in the animals frontend

parts.title: Dashboard cards, summary and actions
parts.scope: The other eleven dashboard rows: inc-014, 015, 016, 002, 025, 026, 027, 028, 029 (blocked) and inc-030, 031 (dropped).
covers: The 9 blocked rows inc-014 (At a glance summary), 015 (card facts), 016 (card date label), 002 (browser tab title), 025 (start button wording), 026 (delete and cancel amendment), 027 (notifications needing action), 028 (drafts on the dashboard), 029 (opening paragraph): each decision.ruling, who ruled and when, and the reason
The 2 dropped rows inc-030 (card links by status) and inc-031 (no unordered list): why each was dropped, from its decision

parts.title: Origin, reason for import and hub
parts.scope: In-scope rows for the origin page, the reason-for-import pages and the notification hub: inc-079, 082, 067, 069, 033 (done), inc-081, 071 (blocked) and inc-043 (rejected).
covers: inc-079 (country code prefix), inc-067 (purpose and exit questions as conditional reveals) and inc-033 (consignment details hub task): every decision and open question in their notes and openQuestions
inc-069 (Exit details hub task) and inc-082 (origin page refuses to save): the reason in failure_reason
inc-081 (Canary Islands, Jersey, French Guiana origins) and inc-071 (port of exit choices): decision.ruling and reason for the block
inc-043 ('Notification tasklist' heading): why it was rejected, from its decision and notes

parts.title: Commodities, identification and documents
parts.scope: In-scope rows for the commodity, animal identification and accompanying documents pages: inc-087, 091, 136, 137, 138 (done), inc-103 (deferred) and inc-094 (dropped).
covers: inc-087 (commodity search), inc-091 (per-species rows for 01061900), inc-136 (document type list), inc-137 (drag and drop upload) and inc-138 (document size limit): every decision and open question in their openQuestions
inc-103 (an animal counts as identified once one identifier is filled): why it was deferred, from its decision
inc-094 (lowering the number of animals below those identified): why it was dropped, from its decision

parts.title: Addresses: permanent address, parties and pickers
parts.scope: The first eight blocked address rows in file order: inc-058, 057, 056, 052, 045, 063, 047, 048. The remaining address and address-book rows are part 7.
covers: The 8 blocked rows inc-058 (permanent address typed in full), 057 (permanent address inside identification), 056 (importer and destination pickers), 052 (addresses list shows only names), 045 ('Consignor or exporter' label), 063 (an option for every unanswered party), 047 (contact address limited to own GB branches), 048 (whole address book on all six pickers): each decision.ruling, who ruled and when, and the reason in decision.note

parts.title: Address book and address picker
parts.scope: The remaining address and address-book rows: inc-053, 065, 046, 064, 054, 055 (blocked) and inc-062 (dropped).
covers: The 6 blocked rows inc-053 (dead end when an address is not saved), 065 (address list heading and caption), 046 (contact-address page explanation), 064 (five-column results table), 054 (correcting a wrong saved address), 055 (whole book on one page, narrowed as you type): each decision.ruling, who ruled and when, and the reason
inc-062 (searchable saved address book): why it was dropped, from its decision

parts.title: Transport and review
parts.scope: In-scope rows for the transport pages and the check-your-answers, declaration and confirmation pages: inc-118, 122, 146, 147, 150, 153 (done), inc-126, 145 (deferred) and inc-127 (blocked).
covers: inc-118 (transit countries one at a time) and inc-122 (transporter list layout): every decision and open question in their openQuestions
inc-126 (duplicate ports) and inc-145 (arrival date label on review): why each was deferred, from its decision
inc-127 (malformed port names): decision.ruling and reason for the block

inc-150 (incomplete notification signal), inc-146 (Change links on a finished notification), inc-147 (numbered review sections) and inc-153 (what is still outstanding after submit): every decision and open question in their openQuestions
